prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes string values before validating them against the field's Pydantic annotation. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both patch the identical conditional in pre_parse_json and would conflict on merge. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated() step before checking the union, so it correctly detects `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` — the idiomatic FastMCP/Pydantic pattern for describing a parameter — as needing the skip. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() calls get_origin() directly on the raw annotation; since get_origin() returns `Annotated` (not the union origin) for an Annotated-wrapped type, is_union_origin() check fails and it falls through to the 'should parse' default, so the corruption bug remains unfixed for any Optional[str] parameter that also carries a Field/description via Annotated, which is a very common real-world shape. #2032's broader _SIMPLE_TYPES set (covering str|int, str|bool, etc.) is more general in the non-Annotated case, but the Annotated-unwrapping gap makes it miss the common case that #3056 explicitly targets and documents.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the identical conditional in pre_parse_json and would conflict on merge. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated() step before checking the union, so it correctly detects `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` — the idiomatic FastMCP/Pydantic pattern for describing a parameter — as needing the skip. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() calls get_origin() directly on the raw annotation; since get_origin() returns `Annotated` (not the union origin) for an Annotated-wrapped type, is_union_origin() check fails and it falls through to the 'should parse' default, so the corruption bug remains unfixed for any Optional[str] parameter that also carries a Field/description via Annotated, which is a very common real-world shape. #2032's broader _SIMPLE_TYPES set (covering str|int, str|bool, etc.) is more general in the non-Annotated case, but the Annotated-unwrapping gap makes it miss the common case that #3056 explicitly targets and documents.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py JSON-decodes string values before validating them against the field's Pydantic annotation. For fields typed as `str | None` (or other unions where `str` is a valid member), this corrupts legitimate string inputs that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a plain string "123" or "[1,2]") by silently converting them to int/list before Pydantic ever sees the original string. Both PRs add a guard before the `json.loads` call in the same `isinstance(data_value, str) and ...` conditional to skip pre-parsing for such union annotations.

clusters.pick_reason: Both patch the identical conditional in pre_parse_json and would conflict on merge. #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated() step before checking the union, so it correctly detects `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` — the idiomatic FastMCP/Pydantic pattern for describing a parameter — as needing the skip. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() calls get_origin() directly on the raw annotation; since get_origin() returns `Annotated` (not the union origin) for an Annotated-wrapped type, is_union_origin() check fails and it falls through to the 'should parse' default, so the corruption bug remains unfixed for any Optional[str] parameter that also carries a Field/description via Annotated, which is a very common real-world shape. #2032's broader _SIMPLE_TYPES set (covering str|int, str|bool, etc.) is more general in the non-Annotated case, but the Annotated-unwrapping gap makes it miss the common case that #3056 explicitly targets and documents.

members.title: fix(shared): preserve MCPError payload on pickle
members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2555: Both PRs patch src/mcp/shared/exceptions.py to fix the same underlying bug: MCPError subclasses (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError) fail to unpickle because the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), and self.args was set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data) — which doesn't match UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message=None) constructor signature, raising a TypeError on every unpickle.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs rewrite the identical cancel() block in session.py from the same base commit, so only one can land as-is. #2493's diff is self-consistent across both files it touches: it removes the response-sending code in session.py AND updates the matching comment/log line in server.py's cancelled branch so the code and its documentation agree. #2514 only edits session.py, leaving server.py's log message/comment referring to 'responder.cancel() already sent an error response' and 'duplicate response suppressed' — text that describes behavior neither PR's session.py change still exhibits, so merging #2514 alone would leave stale/inaccurate comments in server.py.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: RequestResponder.cancel() in src/mcp/shared/session.py unconditionally sends an error response to indicate cancellation. Both PRs are branched from the identical pre-fix blob (session.py hash 243eef5ae6) and rewrite the exact same block in cancel() ('self._cancel_scope.cancel(); self._completed = True; # Send an error response to indicate cancellation'), so they cannot both be applied without a conflict. #2493 deletes that response-sending code outright and updates the corresponding comment/log in server.py's cancelled-exception branch to match ('per spec receivers must not send a response for a cancelled request'). #2514 instead replaces the same block with logic to emit a notifications/cancelled message (new CancelledNotificationParams import) for the request-timeout / caller-cancellation paths, but its diff only touches session.py and leaves server.py's now-superseded 'duplicate response suppressed' comment/log untouched. (2 PRs)
